name: Hare
why: Won 0 of 4.
idea: A walker that runs. Same six spoked legs as the league, but a light frame, full-size motors and a gait driven at more than twice the league's pace, with a steel lance held out ahead. It strikes at a run, where a blow breaks joints, and is gone before the enemy has turned.

name: Lever
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Warden, Mantis), including the champion.
idea: Win the shoving match by taking the enemy's weight. A heavy wheeled machine slides a steel fork under the enemy and lifts: the enemy's feet lose their grip, that weight lands on this machine's front wheels, and it carries the enemy to the edge. Nothing in the league lifts.

name: Wasp
why: Won 0 of 4.
idea: Speed as the weapon. A 430 kg wheeled wedge that goes three times as fast as anything in the league, hits the enemy on the side facing away from the nearest edge, and if the enemy does not give, pulls out and comes again from a new angle instead of leaning on it.

name: Bolt
why: Won 0 of 4.
idea: Wasp from round 1 rebuilt for a small ring, where there is no room to reach top speed: six wheels on full-size motors for pull-away, thick steel axles, and runs that start from seven metres out. A wheeled wedge that hits the enemy on the side facing away from the nearest edge, and if the enemy does not give, pulls out and comes again from a new angle instead of leaning on it.

name: Jab
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Dreadnought, Strider), including the champion.
idea: A boxer that goes for the legs. Every machine in the league stands on spoked legs whose joints are its weakest, and a blow counts by how fast it lands, so this machine carries three piston fists that strike at 8 m/s whatever its own speed. It picks the nearest leg still attached, sets itself at exactly fist range from it, jabs, and steps back out of reach while the fists recharge.

name: Jack
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Dreadnought), including the champion.
idea: Lever from round 1 with the two faults its fights showed put right: axles of thick steel, since Lever lost two of three just landing on rough ground, and a fork that stays under the enemy and keeps carrying instead of letting go after four seconds. Win the shoving match by taking the enemy's weight. A heavy wheeled machine slides a steel fork under the enemy and lifts: the enemy's feet lose their grip, that weight lands on this machine's front wheels, and it carries the enemy to the edge. Nothing in the league lifts.

name: Sparrer
why: Knocked out by Jab in 36.8 s (ring_out).
idea: Jab on legs. Jab's wheels stalled on the hills and it drew two of its four fights standing off. This puts the same three piston fists and the same leg-picking program on the league's six-legged steel frame, to see whether the boxer works on ground that wheels cannot take.

name: Toss
why: Won 2 of 4 (beat Jab, Warden), including the champion.
idea: A flipper, to end the draws. Thick-steel machines shrug off every blow in the league, so this one does not try to break them: it slides three steel pads under the enemy and fires them upward together on geared pistons, 30 kN in all, enough to throw a 700 kg machine off its feet. Then it drives the tumbling machine out before it recovers.

name: Fencer
why: Won 0 of 4.
idea: Reach. A six-legged walker with one piston point on the end of a long steel shaft, 3.5 m ahead of its core and 4.1 m at full thrust, against Jab's 2.5 m. name: Hornet-flank
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Hornet).
idea: Hornet's body with a program that picks its side. It works out where the enemy's weapons are from the enemy's own moving joints, circles to the opposite side at full speed, staying out of reach, and only then runs in. The turret tracks the nearest piece it can actually hit, not the enemy's middle, and it leaves along the same weak side, re-reading the side as the enemy turns.

name: Jab-flank
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Jab), including the champion.
idea: Jab's body with a program that will not step in from the front. It reads where the enemy's weapons are from its moving joints, circles to the other side, and takes only legs on that side, so it boxes from where the enemy cannot answer.

name: Ballista
why: Ballista's control program threw an error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')
idea: A ring-out gun, aimed at Toss. Three geared pistons side by side fire as one: 30 kN for 0.6 m, enough to send an 800 kg machine back at several metres a second. The program does not waste it: it holds fire until the enemy stands between its ram and an edge within reach of the throw, then fires all three. On ten legs and nearly a tonne, so the recoil moves the enemy and not itself.

name: Whirl
why: Knocked out by Toss in 35.2 s (ring_out).
idea: The quick two-wheeled body with a weapon that needs no recharge: a steel bar spinning flat above its wheels. Under the new damage rules only fast contacts count, and the tip of this bar is always fast. It goes round to the enemy's weak side and grazes it with the tip of the bar, keeping its own body a bar's length away.

name: Hornet-shadow
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Dreadnought).
idea: Hornet-flank landed its punches but spent most of each fight running in and out, and drew with Dreadnought after taking four legs. This program does not leave: it takes station just outside the enemy's outermost piece on its weak side, holds there as the enemy turns (it is three times as fast), and punches every time the fist recharges. It gives ground only when one of the enemy's weapons swings to within reach of it.

name: Scythe
why: Knocked out by Toss in 41.2 s (ring_out).
idea: A walker whose weapon is a swept bar, placed by angle. A 2.2 m steel bar is pivoted ahead of its nose at leg height and driven by a motor that goes to the angle it is told. The program cocks the bar out to one side, steps until an enemy leg is inside the arc, and sweeps to the other side, so the bar comes through the legs sideways at over 15 m/s. Then it sweeps back. No pistons to recharge and nothing spinning to tangle.

name: Stoat

Toss's pads only reach forward, so it is built to live on Toss's tail.

name: Scythe-wheels
why: Won 3 of 4 (beat Toss, Scythe, Jab), including the champion.
idea: Scythe only looked for legs, so against a wheeled machine it swept at whatever was nearest, which against Toss was a pad lying under the bar's height. This program treats wheels as legs: it steps in on the nearest wheel or leg and sweeps through that.

name: Stoat-bold

idea: Swift and Jack drew on High ground parked ten metres apart: the shared route-finder refuses a steep slope, so neither went up. This program notices two seconds of standing still out of reach and drives straight at Jack for three, slope or not, braking only for the edge.

name: Toss-skirt
why: Over the mass allowance: 1356.72 kg, the limit is 1200 kg.
idea: Toss with a steel skirt down each side. Reaper, Scythe-wheels and Swift beat wheeled machines by sweeping a low bar through the wheels and taking the axles off with them. The skirts are two thick steel rails outside the wheels at bar height, so the bar meets them first.

name: Jack-arc
why: Won 1 of 4 (beat Mantis), including the champion.
idea: A slow-motion look at the High ground stand-offs showed the cause: a six-wheeled machine with all its wheels on the ground cannot turn on the spot. The tyres grip too well to scrub sideways, so when the way to the enemy is round the hill it sits with its wheels fighting each other. Jack leads on draws because of this. Jack-arc keeps Jack as built and changes the steering: it never asks for a turn on the spot, and turns in a moving arc instead.

name: Pivot
why: Won 4 of 4 (beat Mantis, Jack, Dreadnought, Toss), including the champion.
idea: A slow-motion look at the High ground stand-offs showed the cause: a six-wheeled machine with all its wheels on the ground cannot turn on the spot. The tyres grip too well to scrub sideways, so when the way to the enemy is round the hill it sits with its wheels fighting each other. Pivot is Mower with the middle axle set lower, so it rocks on two wheels and turns freely. Against Mantis that should let it keep its shears pointed at Mantis instead of being walked round and shoved out.
